alternatives.note: The junction already meters the opposing stream. Removing the signal is what creates the gap problem in the first place.

Move it to a chainage where the opposing through flow is lower. Only helps if such a chainage exists within a tolerable detour. It cannot help the 2 bay(s) whose demand is above the 1,800 veh/h a single opening passes at zero opposing traffic, and for the rest the opposing flow would have to fall 91%.

A metered U-turn manufactures the gap the stream will not offer. It reintroduces the signal the scheme exists to remove, on the corridor rather than at the junction. It still cannot serve the 2 bay(s) above the 1,800 veh/h ceiling: metering creates gaps, it does not shorten the follow-up headway.

alternatives.measure: widen the median, add an acceleration lane
alternatives.note: Raises capacity by lowering the follow-up headway and letting vehicles merge rather than cross. A second-order effect on a first-order shortfall. It cannot help the 2 bay(s) whose demand is above the 1,800 veh/h a single opening passes at zero opposing traffic, and for the rest the opposing flow would have to fall 91%.

The only measure that changes the binding term: it removes the conflicting flow rather than asking the U-turn to find gaps in it. For the 2 bay(s) above the ceiling it works by removing the NEED for a U-turn - with the through movement elevated the junction can keep a signalised right turn - not by making the bay work. A single opening still cannot pass their demand.
